issues.legal_issue: Whether property purchased by a husband in his wife's name was held by the wife as its real owner or by the husband as its beneficial owner.
material_facts: The property was purchased with the husband's funds in his wife's name.
The wife’s name appeared as owner in municipal and land revenue records.
The husband managed the property, consistently with the ordinary practice of a husband managing property belonging to his wife.
The surrounding circumstances supported the view that the purchase was intended to secure the wife, rather than to conceal the husband's ownership.
issues.conclusion: The wife was the real owner of the property, although the purchase consideration had been provided by her husband.
issues.legal_principle: The person alleging a benami transaction bears the burden of proving it with definite legal evidence; the apparent purchaser is initially presumed to be the real owner. Intention is determined from the surrounding circumstances, including the source of the purchase money, possession and management, motive, relationship of the parties, custody of title deeds, and subsequent conduct. The source of the purchase money is especially important but is not conclusive. A husband's purchase in his wife's name must also be considered against the historical position of Hindu widows and the recognized practice of providing them security. The Court relied on Jaydayal Poddar v. Mst. Bibi Hazra, Binapani Paul v. Pratima Ghosh, Thakur Bhim Singh v. Thakur Kan Singh, and Kanakarathanammal v. S. Loganatha Mudaliar; it also referred to the explanation to Section 3 of the Benami Transactions (Prohibition) Act, 1988, and the Hindu Women’s Right to Property Act, 1937.

rule.if: benami_title_dispute and property_purchased_in_wifes_name and husband_provided_purchase_money and (widow_security_motive or ownership_records_name_wife) and husband_managed_property

predicates.benami_title_dispute: The proceeding involves a dispute over whether a property purchase in one person's name was benami for another person.
predicates.property_purchased_in_wifes_name: A husband purchased the property in his wife's name.
predicates.husband_provided_purchase_money: The husband supplied the money used to purchase the property.
predicates.widow_security_motive: The circumstances support that the purchase was intended to provide security for the wife in light of her position as a widow under the law then prevailing.
predicates.ownership_records_name_wife: Official property records named the wife as the owner.
predicates.husband_managed_property: The husband managed the property on behalf of his wife.

issues.definition: When a benami title dispute concerns property purchased by a husband in his wife's name, and the purchase, its purpose, the ownership records, and the husband's management support her ownership, the wife is treated as the real owner even if he supplied the purchase money.

issues.legal_issue: Whether an alleged adoption affecting succession was established by the evidence presented.
material_facts: The adoption claim was supported by the claimant's testimony and that of one other witness whose evidence the Court found inherently inconsistent and unreliable.
Three deceased witnesses' testimony from an earlier suit was offered in corroboration, but the controversy over the adoption had already arisen when that testimony was recorded.
A letter describing its sender in a way said to indicate the adoption did not permit a clear or firm conclusion that the adoption had occurred.
The claimant's evidence, once the other material was rejected or found inconclusive, stood isolated.
issues.conclusion: The alleged adoption was not proved.
issues.legal_principle: Because adoption changes the course of succession and may divert property, evidence supporting it must be consistent and sufficiently reliable to leave no reasonable doubt. Courts must exercise caution where an adoption is supported only by oral evidence, particularly where suspicious circumstances exist or there is no registered document or other clinching evidence; the person asserting the adoption must dispel such suspicion. The Court relied on Kishori Lal v. Mst. Chaltibai and Rahasa Pandiani v. Gokulananda Panda.

predicates.adoption_claim_affecting_succession: A party claims an adoption that would affect the course of succession to property.
predicates.supporting_testimony_unreliable: The testimony offered to establish the adoption is unreliable because of material inconsistencies or other deficiencies.
predicates.no_clinching_admissible_corroboration: No admissible and conclusive corroborating evidence establishes that the adoption occurred.

issues.definition: If an adoption claim affecting succession rests on unreliable testimony without conclusive admissible corroboration, the adoption is not proved.

issues.legal_issue: Whether testimony from deceased witnesses recorded in an earlier proceeding was admissible to prove the alleged adoption when the controversy had already arisen.
material_facts: Testimony from three witnesses who had since died was recorded in another suit and offered to support the adoption claim.
The controversy concerning whether the adoption had occurred already existed when those witnesses gave their testimony.
issues.conclusion: The earlier testimony was inadmissible to prove the adoption.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 32(5) and (6) of the Evidence Act, a statement relied on under those provisions must have been made ante litem motam: before the commencement not only of legal proceedings but also of any actual controversy concerning the same subject. The Court relied on Kalindindi Venkata Subbaraju v. Chintalapati Subbaraju.

predicates.evidence_offered_to_prove_adoption: A party offers a deceased person's earlier statement as evidence of an alleged adoption.
predicates.declarants_are_dead: The persons who made the earlier statements have died.
predicates.statement_made_after_controversy_arose: The statements were made after an actual or legal controversy concerning the adoption had begun.

issues.definition: When deceased persons' earlier statements are offered to prove an adoption but were made after the controversy arose, those statements are inadmissible.

issues.legal_issue: Whether the court needed to determine the validity of a claimed successor's adoption and a gift to that successor when the party challenging them had no subsisting preferential claim to the property.
material_facts: The property was held to belong to the deceased owner's wife, and the alleged adoption of the claimant's husband was not proved.
On the resulting succession, the property devolved on the deceased owner's daughter.
If the claimed successor's adoption were invalid, another heir had a better or preferential claim than the claimant to succeed to the daughter's property.
That heir did not challenge the claimed adoption; the claimant's challenge therefore could not establish a right to the property.
The claimed successor's adoption and the gift in that person's favour were consequently unnecessary to resolve the claimant's appeal.
issues.conclusion: The court was justified in not deciding the validity of the claimed successor's adoption or the gift, because those questions were redundant and inconsequential to the claimant's entitlement.
issues.legal_principle: Where the party raising a challenge has no subsisting right to the property and a different heir would have the better claim if the challenged succession were invalid, determining the validity of that succession or a related gift is unnecessary to resolve that party's claim.

rule.if: property_succession_dispute and challenger_lacks_preferential_entitlement and another_heir_has_better_claim and better_heir_did_not_challenge

predicates.property_succession_dispute: The proceeding concerns competing claims to property through succession.
predicates.challenger_lacks_preferential_entitlemen: The party challenging a claimed successor has no subsisting entitlement that would allow the party to take the property.
predicates.another_heir_has_better_claim: A different heir would have a better or preferential claim if the claimed successor's adoption were invalid.
predicates.better_heir_did_not_challenge: The heir with the better or preferential claim did not challenge the claimed successor's adoption.

issues.definition: In a property succession dispute, if the challenger lacks a preferential entitlement and a better-placed heir has not challenged the claimed succession, related adoption and gift questions need not be decided.
